paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, and I'm not going to hurry past it. God set Jerusalem in the center of the nations, and she rebelled against His ordinances more wickedly than the nations around her (Ezekiel 5:5-6). They hadn't even lived up to the ordinances of the nations around them (Ezekiel 5:7). The more a people have been given, the more it matters what they do with it.

Here's what I want you to hold onto. God didn't spring this on anybody. He had Ezekiel act it out with a razor and a set of scales, a sign nobody could miss, and then He spelled it out in plain words. He says of Jerusalem, "Behold, I Myself am against you," and He closes with "I, the LORD, have spoken" (Ezekiel 5:8, 17). I think a God who says it that clearly is a God who means every word.

So what do you do with it, baker? Take it seriously, and don't coast. God's words aren't background noise, and His warnings are as real as His promises. Come back to His Word with an open heart, and keep your ovens ready. This story isn't over, and neither is what God has to say.
